```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../../../../private/research-findings/quarto")
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from runflow.results import read_gaussian_checkpoint, xyz_frames
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from molstarview import MolstarViewer
from calculations import LABELS, PLOT_LABELS, Calculation

_calculation = Calculation("../../../../../private/research-findings/projects/2026-10-15_225958/2026-10-15_225959/2026-10-16_105709")
register_plot_labels(PLOT_LABELS)
_calculation_icons = {True: "![Yes](../../../../../private/research-findings/projects/icons/check.svg){.workflow-status}", False: "![No](../../../../../private/research-findings/projects/icons/cross.svg){.workflow-status}", "Warning": "![Warning](../../../../../private/research-findings/projects/icons/warning.svg){.workflow-status}", "Error": "![Error](../../../../../private/research-findings/projects/icons/cross.svg){.workflow-status}"}


def _calculation_table(data, precision=5):
    """Render a table of codename columns under their labels, with booleans as status icons."""
    data = data.map(lambda value: _calculation_icons[value] if isinstance(value, bool) else value)
    display(Markdown(scientific_table(data.rename(columns=LABELS), precision=precision)))
```

## Warnings and errors

Every warning and error parsed from the program output and the runflow script records, with where it comes from and its physical or numerical reason.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.findings_table(_calculation_icons))
```

## Calculation overview

The program, the resources and the timing of the calculation.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.overview())
```

## Gaussian input

### Link 0 commands

The Link 0 commands set the job's memory, processors and files before the route; each is explained after the Gaussian manual.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.link0_table(1))
```

### Route keywords and options

The route selects the method, basis set and job type. Each keyword is listed with its meaning, followed by its options, as Gaussian read them.

::: {.grouped-table}
```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.route_table(1))
```

:::

### Molecule specification

The job's title, charge and spin multiplicity, and where Gaussian took its geometry from.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.molecule_table(1))
```

### Starting geometry

The structure the calculation starts from, as the first geometry Gaussian printed.

```{python}
display(MolstarViewer(_calculation.geometry_frame()))
```

::: {.fold}
#### Starting coordinates

Cartesian coordinates of every atom.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.coordinates_table())
```

:::

## Gaussian output

### Electronic system and solvent

The size of the electronic problem Gaussian set up for this geometry and basis set, with the solvent model where the job uses one.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.system_table(1))
```

### SCF convergence

The job converged 8 self-consistent field solutions, one per geometry or state it evaluated, each with its final energy, number of cycles and remaining RMS density change. Every SCF uses `RPM6D3`. Convergence is marked on the first SCF and wherever it changes.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.scf_table(1), precision=12)
```

The number of cycles each SCF needed, against its index.

```{python}
display_chart(_calculation.scf_chart(1), zoom_axes=('x',))
```

### Geometry optimization

The geometry optimization took 8 steps. The first plot shows the energy relative to the final step; the second divides each of Gaussian's four convergence criteria by its threshold, so a step converges when all four fall below the dashed line at 1.

```{python}
_energy, _criteria = _calculation.optimization_charts(1)
display_chart(_energy, zoom_axes=('x',))
display_chart(_criteria, zoom_axes=('x',))
```

::: {.fold}
#### Optimization steps

Every step with its energy and the four criteria.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.optimization_table(1), precision=12)
```

:::

### Geometries along the job

Every geometry Gaussian printed during the job, in order; the viewer steps through them, trailed by faded copies of the preceding geometries.

```{python}
display(MolstarViewer(_calculation.trajectory(1)))
```

### Vibrational frequencies

The harmonic analysis gave 84 modes, 3 of them imaginary. The stick spectrum places each mode's infrared intensity at its wavenumber, imaginary modes at negative wavenumbers.

```{python}
display_chart(_calculation.ir_chart(1), zoom_axes=('x',))
```

The viewer animates every imaginary mode, the six lowest real modes and the four most intense in the infrared, each with a largest atomic excursion of 0.6 $\mathrm{\AA}$; choose one in its snapshot selector. Faded copies spread over the mode's frames trail the motion; the trail button on the right toolbar hides them.

```{python}
_frames, _names = _calculation.mode_frames(1)
display(MolstarViewer(_frames, names=_names))
```

::: {.fold}
#### Normal modes

Every mode with its reduced mass, force constant and infrared intensity, and its symmetry when the molecule has any.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.modes_table(1))
```

:::

### Thermochemistry

Gaussian's ideal-gas, rigid-rotor and harmonic-oscillator thermochemistry at the stated temperature and pressure: the thermal corrections and the corrected energies.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.thermochemistry_table(1))
```

::: {.fold}
#### Thermal contributions

Thermal energy, heat capacity and entropy from the electronic, translational, rotational and vibrational contributions.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.thermal_components(1))
```

:::

### Frontier orbitals

The frontier orbital energies of the final SCF and their gap, an orbital-energy difference rather than an excitation energy.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.frontier_table(1))
```

The canonical orbital energies around the gap.

```{python}
display_chart(_calculation.orbitals_chart(1), zoom_axes=('y',))
```

### Atomic charges and dipole

The Mulliken atomic charges of the last population analysis, blue where positive and red where negative.

```{python}
display_chart(_calculation.charges_chart(1))
```

The dipole moment of the same density, by component and in magnitude.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.dipole_table(1))
```

### Static polarizability

The static dipole polarizability tensor $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ from the job's last complete response calculation: each element is the dipole induced along one axis by a unit field along another.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.polarizability_table(1))
```

### Gaussian archive entry

The archive entry is Gaussian's own summary, printed when the job ends normally. Its energies are rounded; the SCF table holds the precise values.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.archive_table(1))
```

::: {.fold}
### Parsing coverage

Every category of output runflow recognises: whether the route requested it and whether runflow decoded it from the log, marked with a cross where it decoded only part, with the number of records it read.

```{python}
_calculation_table(_calculation.coverage_table(1))
```

:::

## Checkpoint structures and electronic data

Retained formatted checkpoints show the saved geometry and electronic state. They are snapshots, rather than a complete history of every intermediate checkpoint write.

### Starting checkpoint 1

```{python}
_checkpoint_path = Path('../../../../../private/research-findings/') / 'projects/2026-10-15_225958/2026-10-15_225959/2026-10-15_230000/checkpoints/indigo-carbon-barrier.fchk'
_checkpoint = read_gaussian_checkpoint(_checkpoint_path)
_calculation_table(_calculation.checkpoint_table(_checkpoint_path))
display(MolstarViewer(xyz_frames(_checkpoint.numbers, _checkpoint.coordinates[None, :, :])) )
_orbitals = _calculation.checkpoint_orbitals(_checkpoint_path)
if _orbitals is not None:
    display_chart(_orbitals)
if _checkpoint.irc is not None:
    display(MolstarViewer(_checkpoint.irc.frames))
if _checkpoint.vibrations is not None:
    _v = _checkpoint.vibrations
    _calculation_table(pd.DataFrame(dict(mode=range(1, len(_v.frequencies)+1), frequency=_v.frequencies.to('1/cm').magnitude, intensity=_v.intensities.to('km/mol').magnitude)).head(10))
```
